texts: The old emperor's golden barge and my grandfather's fishing boat both rotted at the same pier, and the emperor's treasure lock rusted shut; write a doha about that.
boat, lock, rulers
doha pls: a king's boat sinks like anyone's, and his locks can't keep death out
Write a doha saying that a king may keep his treasure behind a hundred locks and sail in the grandest boat, but the day death arrives, his locks open and his boat turns back at the shore.
A hundred locks guard the king's chest, yet one breath unlocks his end; the boat of power drifts to the same shore as the fisherman's.
tree, ruler, mortal
The king planted a tree at his coronation, and today the tree stands over his forgotten grave; write a doha.
doha pls: a king is like a tree, strong for a season, then it falls
Proud stands the tree in the king's garden, and prouder stood the king; both bow to the same wind in time.
Compose a doha that says the ruler who sits proudly in his court is like a great tree, shading many for a time, but with one season's change the tree falls and nobody remembers its name.
I visited the royal cremation site, where the ash of a great emperor lay mixed with the ash of his servants and the milk poured over it was for all; write a doha.
doha pls: kings turn to ash like everyone, they can't buy milk or mercy from death
ash, milk, mortal kings
The king who bathed in milk each morning is a handful of ash; the poor man's ash is the same.
Please craft a couplet saying that a king who was bathed in milk and wrapped in silk turns to ash like the pauper who drank from the road, and the one who made both asks only for their deeds.
The governor who made our village tremble for thirty years died last month, and the funeral was no bigger than a farmer's; write a doha about it.
mighty men die
doha pls: rulers die just like their subjects, why do they act so proud
The mighty and the meek are measured by the same span of years, and carried by the same last journey.
I want a doha that says no ruler, however feared, can buy a single extra breath with his authority, and that when his time comes he leaves everything behind exactly as the poorest of his subjects do.
Write a doha showing that a king may command armies and press a whole province's labour through his tax collectors like an oil press, yet cannot press even one hour more from his own life.
The oil press squeezes the poor for the king's treasury... yet the king himself is squeezed by time.
The tax collectors of our ruler worked us like an oil press for years, and then he fell ill and no amount of money could squeeze out another day; write a doha.
oil press, ruler, tax
doha pls: a king uses the people like an oil press, but death presses the king too
The king's cloth sheet is woven with gilded strands, the beggar's of rags, yet when the night comes both are laid out upon the same earth.
Write a doha saying that a king may wear fine robes and the beggar a torn cloth sheet, but when death comes the king can neither bargain nor beg for another day of rule.
doha pls: a king and a beggar both end up under the same cloth sheet in the end
I saw a beggar and a rich lord covered with the same plain cloth sheet at the cremation, and the thought stayed with me; write a doha.
beggar, king, cloth sheet
The temple bows to the king's gift as it does to the poor man's flower, and the Lord looks only at the heart that comes.
temple, forehead mark, king
doha pls: a king can put a big forehead mark on at the temple but God still sees only the heart
Make me a doha that says the king may build a temple and receive a forehead mark from the holy men, but the Lord cannot be bought with gifts, and the ruler stands before Him as bare as a pauper.
The local lord donated a huge amount to the temple and expected special blessings, with a big forehead mark and all, and I thought the Lord must smile at such bargaining; write a doha.
mountain, ruler's pride
doha pls: a king can't climb the mountain of God with wealth
The king may stand upon the mountain's crest and call it his, yet the mountain was there before him and will be after.
Please write a doha that says the proudest ruler is as small as an ant beneath a mountain, and the mountain too will fall one day, so his pride in his throne is just a short-lived dream.
I stood with my grandfather on a high mountain pass where an old conqueror's fort lies in ruins, and he said, see how the mountain outlived the king; write a doha.
tongue, spinning wheel, king
The king's tongue commands a thousand men, yet the spinning wheel of time turns, and the tongue falls silent.
doha pls: the king's tongue gives orders but time's spinning wheel will wind him up too
The old king whose tongue could send men to prison now lies silent in his bed, and the spinning wheel in the corner, left by his mother, still hums; write a doha.
Write a doha that says the ruler whose tongue once made nations tremble will find that the spinning wheel of fate winds out his own life just as it does a pauper's, and no command can stop it.
doha pls: a king's sword can conquer lands but not death, and a bier waits for him too
Can you make a doha that says the king may win a hundred battles with his sword and rule many lands, but the bier is made ready for him as for any man, and no army can stand against it.
sword, bier, king
The general who swore he would never be conquered died in his sleep and was carried on a plain bier with his sword by his side; write a doha.
Though his sword conquer the world, the king rests at last upon the bier, and the sword he wielded lies idle.
The mighty rule a season, the Lord rules always; bow, O ruler, to the one who bows to none.
doha pls: rulers think they are in charge but the real boss is God
power is borrowed
Our village head lost the election after twenty years of bossing us around and now sits in the corner of the tea stall, humbled; write a doha.
I want a doha that says authority in this world is merely lent to people for a short time, and the wise ruler uses it with humility, for he too must account for himself before the real Ruler.
We saw the stars over the ruined fort where a great king once ruled, and my father said the stars saw him come and go; write a doha.
stars, ruler, mortal
Write a doha saying that the stars have witnessed countless rulers boasting of their power on earth, and not one of them could carry even a single acre with him when he went beyond.
The stars have watched a hundred kings arise and fall, and still they shine, unbowed and unimpressed.
doha pls: stars have seen so many kings come and go, ours will pass too
The cloud passed over the great ruler's fort and rained as much on the farmer's field; write a doha.
The cloud rains alike on the king's courtyard and the poor man's lane, caring nothing for either's name.
doha pls: a cloud doesn't care who is king, rain falls the same
Compose a doha showing that a cloud drifts across the sky and does not pause to honour a king's rule, since the Maker's gifts fall equally on all, and no ruler can command the rain by his might.
cloud, king, powerless
The physician of the king gave him medicines made with rare herbs and gave his forehead a sacred mark, but the king still died at fifty; write a doha.
doha pls: a king's physician can't cure death, even with a forehead mark and blessing
Pen a doha that says the royal physician may treat the king with the rarest medicines and the holy men may bless him with a mark on the forehead, but when his time is up nothing can add to it.
physician, forehead mark, king
The physician bows before the king, but he bows before death too; the mark on the forehead cannot stay the hand of time.
The palace is the king's pride, and the weaver's loom the poor man's hope; death walks into both without knocking.
palace, weaver's loom, king
Compose a doha showing that a king may live in a palace of marble and the weaver sit at his simple loom, but both are lodgers in this world, and the Lord, who owns all, will ask both to leave.
My grandfather, who wove at his loom, once worked in the king's palace repairing the carpets, and he told me the king feared death more than he did; write a doha.
doha pls: a palace is a grand place but even the king has to leave it, same as a weaver leaves his loom
Please write a doha about how the stars and the moon watch the kings of the earth struggle over land and treasure, then watch their funerals one by one, and the heavens remain calm and unmoved.
Last night under the moon and the stars, I read about the endless wars of emperors, and wondered what is left of them; write a doha.
stars, moon, rulers
doha pls: the moon and stars have seen kings die for ages, what's one more
The moon and the stars have seen the throne grow cold a thousand times, and still they keep their watch.
The old potter who sat by his wheel making clay pots told me that the king's body too would return to clay, like the pots he made; write a doha.
I want a doha that says the king and the potter's pot are made of the same clay, and just as the pot breaks and returns to the earth, the king's body turns to dust and his power is forgotten.
doha pls: kings are made of the same clay as the potter's pots, and break just as easily
The potter shapes the king's cup and the pauper's from one clay, and both return to dust when broken.
potter, clay, king
rulers must die
Heavy is the burden of rule, yet lighter than the weight that comes at the end.
I want a doha that says that emperors and chiefs, no matter how many men bow before them, cannot bargain with death for a single day, and in that moment their power is of no use at all.
doha pls: no matter how powerful, everyone dies
The most powerful man in our district died in a car accident at forty, with all his security and wealth beside him; write a doha.
The merchant prince who spent his life chasing the philosopher's stone, as people say, died alone while a fly buzzed on his empty cup; write a doha.
With the philosopher's stone in his chest the king is still a supplicant at the Lord's gate, and the fly rests freely on a flower.
Write a doha that says even if the king had the philosopher's stone and could turn all things to treasure, he could not buy the Lord, and a fly that sits freely on a flower is more content than he.
doha pls: a king may have the philosopher's stone but even a fly has more freedom than him
philosopher's stone, fly, king
power cannot buy God

Compose a doha that says a ruler may buy armies, loyalty and jaggery-sweet flattery, but the Lord cannot be purchased with any wealth, since He looks only for love and humility in the heart of whoever approaches Him.
doha pls: kings enjoy sweet jaggery-like praise, but God isn't impressed
The flatterers' praise is sweet to the king as jaggery, yet it dissolves in the mouth of death.
My uncle, a minister, was surrounded by sycophants who offered him sweets and praise, and when he fell from office, only one person remained; write a doha.
I'd like a doha that says a king stands at the crossroads of life like any commoner, a moneylender with his purse beside him cannot buy a way past death, and each must take the road meant for him.
At the crossroads the king and the moneylender wait alike, and the road they take is not of their choosing.
At the crossroads outside our town, a moneylender's carriage and a farmer's cart were stuck behind a funeral procession of an old ruler; write a doha.
crossroads, moneylender, king
doha pls: king or moneylender, at the crossroads of death no one gets priority
The shadow of the throne is long at evening and gone at night; so is the shadow of every ruler.
The shadow of the governor's grand building fell across our little lane for years, and last month they pulled it down; write a doha.
shadow, ruler's power
doha pls: a king's shadow stretches long but disappears at night
Please write a doha showing that the power of a ruler is like a shadow that grows long at evening, and disappears in the dark of death, leaving nothing behind that he can call his own.
The mighty man's name is proudly proclaimed, yet the Lord's name is written in the heart that kneels.
Compose a doha that says the ruler who builds monuments to his glory and orders chants of praise cannot escape the court of the Lord, where only humility and good deeds are counted.
My uncle, a district official, always insisted on being addressed as sir by everyone, and after retirement he sits alone and nobody greets him; write a doha.
pride falls
doha pls: powerful people lose it all eventually, so don't be proud
ocean, king, small
The emperor who tried to command the tide and order it back stood in the ocean spray, soaking wet and humbled; I read it as a story and I'd love a doha out of it.
doha pls: a king can't order the ocean, and can't order God either
The ocean ignores the king's decree, and the Lord ignores the king's wealth; both roll on, indifferent to pride.
Give me a doha that says the ruler stands before the ocean like a child, for his army cannot hold back the waves, nor bribe them, and before the Lord he is smaller than a grain of dust.
Please write a doha that says the king may eat the finest food and still need a pinch of salt to taste it, just as the poor do, since both are sustained by the same Giver and bound to leave.
doha pls: salt makes the king's food tasty just like the poor man's, no difference
The royal cook told me that even the king's feast needs a pinch of salt, or he would throw it away; it made me smile, write a doha.
The king's golden plate and the potter's bowl both beg a pinch of salt; the Giver gives it to both alike.
salt, king, humble
The cleric blesses the ruler, and the ruler lights a lamp at the shrine, but the Lord sees through the show.
The governor made a public show of lighting a lamp in front of a cleric, but his tax collectors robbed the poor that very day; write a doha.
Compose a doha that says a ruler may seek the blessing of a cleric and light a lamp for the crowd, but pomp and wealth cannot buy the Lord, who looks only into the quiet heart.
doha pls: kings flaunt their devotion with a cleric and a lamp, but God isn't fooled
cleric, lamp, ruler
The swan has no throne or treasure, yet drifts across the royal lake with more dignity than the king himself, I thought; write a doha.
The king rules the lake by edict, the swan by grace; only one is truly free.
Please craft a couplet that says the swan on the royal lake is freer than the king who owns it, because the king is bound by fear, desire and ambition, and the swan owns nothing and loses nothing.
swan, king, free
doha pls: the swan on the king's lake is freer than the king
The king ordered a spotless cloth sheet to be laid out for his bed and the same cloth sheet was spread over him a year later; write a doha.
A cloth sheet beneath the king in the night, a cloth sheet above the king in the grave.
cloth sheet, king

Compose a doha showing that the king who sleeps on the finest cloth sheet will rest one day beneath the plainest one, and the same earth that welcomes the poor welcomes him with no sign of his greatness.
doha pls: kings sleep on fancy cloth sheets but they all end up under a plain one

Please compose a doha that says the powerful man who bullies the weak should remember that every power is borrowed, and when it is taken back, he will stand before the Lord as small as those he bullied.
My boss loved throwing his weight around until he was fired, and now he asks for favours from the people he used to shout at; write a doha.
power is temporary
doha pls: abusing power backfires, everyone ends up the same
Those who tread on the weak today shall be trodden by time tomorrow; borrowed strength must be returned.
doha pls: a king's river of wealth dries up like any stream
Make me a doha saying that the king's treasures flow in like a river during his rule and drain away the moment he dies, since not one coin can cross the great river that every soul must cross.
The old emperor's treasury was emptied by his sons within a month of his death, like a river that ran dry after the monsoon; write a doha.
river, king, wealth fades
The river of the king's wealth is wide in spring and dry in the hour of his passing.
Compose a doha that says the king is a leaf in the great garden of life, which looks green and mighty in the season but yellows and falls in autumn, scattered without a trace of its glory.
doha pls: a king is just a leaf in the wind of time
leaf, king
I watched a single leaf blow across the courtyard of the ruined royal fort, and thought of the kings who had walked there; write a doha.
The leaf that rests on the king's lap and the leaf that falls on the poor man fall to the same earth.
The king gazes in the mirror and sees a ruler; the Lord sees a mortal like all the rest.
mirror, heron, king
Write a doha that says the king who looks into the mirror and admires his own face, like a heron admiring its reflection, must know that the Lord sees him as the same fragile being as any other.
The emperor's mirror was as tall as a man, and he spent his mornings admiring himself like a heron on a bank; his funeral was short and quiet, write a doha.
doha pls: a king admires himself in the mirror like a heron, but death sees him as ordinary
The chairman of our company, who once ruled over thousands, died alone in a hospital room and only a few employees attended; write a doha.
rulers fade
I want a doha that says those who rule over many people and wield great authority should remember that they too stand in the same line as the poorest, waiting for the same call from the Lord.
The ruler's word has force while he lives, and it is dust on the day he passes.
doha pls: power ends when life ends
doha pls: a king crosses the bridge in a grand procession but the bridge to the next world has no special lane for kings

Can you make a doha that says the king rides across the bridge in splendour, dressed in cotton fine as air, but the bridge between this world and the next admits all alike, and the Lord's toll is only humility.
I stood on an old bridge, where a king's procession once crossed in cotton robes, and thought how all have to cross the last bridge alone; write a doha.
bridge, cotton, king
Over the bridge in cotton robes the king rides; over the last bridge he walks on foot like the poor.
doha pls: a king may have a bee-like army of servants but death swallows him like the ocean swallows a stream
Round the king the bees of flattery hum, and the ocean of time waits to swallow the hive.
bee, ocean, king
The king's courtiers buzzed around him like bees till the end, but at his death they dispersed, and the ocean of time closed over his name; write a doha.
Compose a doha that says a king surrounded by flatterers buzzing like bees thinks himself secure, yet the ocean of time will swallow him and his court, and the flatterers will buzz around another.
Power sits upon the mighty like a borrowed robe, and the owner will one day ask for it back.
The minister who once decided the fate of thousands now begs for a seat in a government hospital queue; write a doha.
power is borrowed
doha pls: no one stays in power forever
Please write a doha that says the high office, the title and the authority that a ruler wears are not truly his, for the Lord lends them for a season, and the wise ruler wears them lightly.
The one who commands millions cannot command his own last breath; ask him, and he bows.
I want a doha that says the ruler who commands armies and ministers, who is obeyed in every word, discovers at the end that he has no command over his own breath, which belongs to the Lord.
doha pls: kings can't order their own breath
rulers can't command death
My grandfather, the village chief, used to order everyone around, but at his last hour he couldn't even ask for water without whispering to his grandchild; write a doha.

Pen a doha that says the king may receive a forehead mark at his coronation and plant seeds of fear and power across his realm, yet the only seed the Lord counts is the one planted by kindness and humility.
doha pls: a king may wear a forehead mark and sow seeds of power but God only counts the seeds of good
A forehead mark is placed upon the king; a seed of good is placed in the heart of the humble, and the Lord tends only that seed.
At the coronation of the new ruler of our region, they put a forehead mark on him and planted a seed in the royal garden, and my grandmother murmured that the Lord would judge both; write a doha.
forehead mark, seed, king
crow, bier, king
doha pls: the crow doesn't care if it's a king's bier, it eats like any other
Write a doha that says the crow will perch on a king's bier as easily as on a pauper's, and its cry over a ruler's funeral is the same as over anyone's, proving that death honours no rank.
A crow calls over the king's bier as over any other, caring nothing for his titles.
After the old ruler's bier was carried to the ground, a crow settled on the empty chair where he once sat; write a doha.
doha pls: a king may own a forest but cannot own his next breath
The forest is the king's hunting ground, yet in the end the king is the hunted.

Please write a doha that says the king may claim a whole forest for his hunt, and none may enter it without his leave, yet death enters his chamber without asking and takes him away from all that he owns.
forest, king, mortal
The ruler's hunting forest is now a village school's field, and children play where he once hunted; write a doha.
doha pls: rich and mighty people are as mortal as the poor

I want a doha that says the wealthy and powerful may feel secure behind their guards and wealth, but death is not impressed, and the Lord, who owns all, will ask them for an account like everyone else.
The mighty walk guarded by a hundred, yet no guard can stand between them and the end.
The billionaire in our city died of a heart attack while at his gym, with three bodyguards beside him who could do nothing; write a doha.
wealth can't stop death
What good is a ruler's might, when the call of the Lord comes, and what can he offer in return?
power can't buy God
doha pls: you can't bribe God like you bribe officers
I watched a corrupt official offer a huge donation at a prayer ceremony, as if God could be bought like a clerk, and I felt sad; write a doha.
I want a doha that says the Lord is not a clerk who can be bribed, and the powerful man who thinks he can win His grace with gifts and display has understood neither power nor the Lord.
doha pls: kings forget they are mortal
I overheard a minister's aide say that his boss had never once spoken of death, as if it didn't apply to him, and I wanted a doha about it.
The ruler counts his years like coins, forgetting that the Lord has already counted them.
Compose a doha that says the powerful man behaves as though he will live forever, making plans for centuries, while death stands patiently at his shoulder, waiting for the day his time runs out.
rulers forget death
musk deer, sand, king

Write a doha that says the king hunts the musk deer for its fragrance but cannot find the fragrance in his own heart, and his kingdom, like sand running through his fingers, slips away as he grasps it.
The king hunted a musk deer for sport, and by the time he returned, his kingdom had slipped away like sand through an hourglass; write a doha.
The musk deer carries its fragrance, the king his crown; both are hunted, both are lost like sand.
doha pls: a king hunts the musk deer but the sand of time takes his kingdom
I'd like a doha that says the tongue of a ruler may order men to prison or to glory, but the rainbird, waiting only for the Lord's rain, is wiser, because it asks nothing of the world.
tongue, rainbird, ruler
The tongue of the king commands, the rainbird waits for the sky; one is a master, the other is free.
The king's herald announced decrees all day, while a rainbird sat on the courtyard wall, calling for rain; the bird, I think, was the wiser; write a doha.
doha pls: a king's tongue commands, but the rainbird depends only on God, who is greater
mighty are mortal
Great names are loudly spoken today; in time, they are quietly forgotten.
My grandmother used to say that the strongest man in the village was carried out just as quietly as the weakest; write a doha.
I want a doha that says every ruler, general and landlord who frightened people in life is reduced in the end to silence, equal to those he frightened, and what remains is only his deeds.
doha pls: rulers, however strong, can't escape the end
I saw a lotus bloom in a royal tank in the middle of the sand, which outlasted the kingdom of the ruler who dug it; write a doha.
Write a doha that says the king builds ponds and gardens to be remembered, but sand covers them all, and only the lotus of good deeds blooms on, untouched by time, in the memory of the people.
The kingdom is a footprint in the sand, the lotus is the Lord's gift; one is washed away and the other blooms.
sand, lotus, king
doha pls: kingdoms get buried in sand but good deeds bloom like lotus
doha pls: kings can't take anything with them when they go
nothing goes along
The mighty arrive with empty hands and leave with empty hands; the in-between is all borrowed.
When the old landlord died, his sons spent a week fighting over the property he couldn't take with him; write a doha.

Please write a doha showing that a powerful man who has gathered fields, fortunes and fame for a lifetime finds, on the last day, that he must leave every single thing behind and go as bare as he came.

Give me a doha that says the king's elephant may carry him in splendour and his scales may weigh coins, but the scales of the Lord weigh only deeds, and there a pauper's honesty outweighs the king's pomp.
The ruler's elephant was proud and his scales of justice were crooked; both fell on the same day when the people rose up. Write a doha.
doha pls: a king's elephant is grand but God's scales weigh only deeds
The elephant carries the king, the scales weigh the coin; the Lord's scales weigh the heart.
elephant, scales, king
doha pls: kings think they're gods but they're only human
mere mortals

Compose a doha that says the ruler who lets people kneel before him and call him lord should remember that he is only a servant of the true Lord, subject to the same laws of birth and death as everyone.
The new mayor started demanding that people bow to him and call him sir, though everyone knew he was the grocer's son just two years ago; write a doha.
He who is bowed to by many must remember: the Lord bows to none, and all bow to Him.
